description:
Somos un equipo apasionado por el desarrollo de software, la programación y la exploración humana. Nuestro objetivo es diseñar e implementar un software de monitoreo de salud innovador, eficiente y confiable para astronautas en misiones espaciales de larga duración. Nos motiva resolver problemas complejos donde la tecnología impacta directamente en el bienestar y la seguridad de la tripulación.

Buscamos integrar integrantes dinámicos y comprometidos que quieran sumar su talento al proyecto.
summary:
Orbit Care is an offline-first, autonomous health monitoring and clinical decision-support software developed by team Los Classics for long-duration spaceflight. Grounded in NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) framework, it addresses the five hazards of human spaceflight (space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile closed environments).

Because crewmembers are not always physicians and deep-space missions introduce severe communication delays, Orbit Care empowers non-medical astronauts to assess, prevent, and respond to emergencies independently. The platform integrates an interactive 16-segment 3D anatomical scanner, real-time ECG and respiratory waveform telemetry, color-coded triage alerts, dynamic longitudinal trend charts, a confidential PHQ-9 mental health check-in with physiological coherence validation, and a Pre-EVA operational readiness gate. By translating complex biomedical data into plain-language step-by-step protocols, Orbit Care safeguards crew health across orbital stations, transit spacecraft, rovers, and planetary bases.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Orbit Care is a modular, browser-based biomedical platform that operates completely offline using local persistent state synchronization. It continuously evaluates astronaut health across four selectable mission profiles—Orbital Station (ISS/Gateway), Deep-Space Transit (Orion), Pressurized Rover, and Lunar/Martian Base—automatically recalibrating environmental limits (CO2, radiation exposure in mSv, and Earth communication latency).

• 3D Anatomical Triage (SC-16): Users interact with a rotatable 3D human hologram divided into 16 anatomical zones. Each zone displays a live color-coded status (Optimal, Caution, Critical) linked to spaceflight-specific pathologies (such as Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome [SANS], orthostatic intolerance, bone demineralization, and renal stone risk) alongside 4-step plain-language instructions for non-medical crew.

• Multimodal Data Ingestion & Live Vitals: The system processes keyboard inputs (blood glucose in mg/dL, blood pressure, temperature, sleep hours), mouse/touch interactions (a 15-second pulse and 30-second respiration tactile timer when wearable vests are off), and camera/file uploads (ocular ultrasound frames analyzed for optic nerve sheath dilation ONSD > 5.0 mm).

• Behavioral Health & Coherent Privacy: To counter isolation and confinement, astronauts complete a confidential 9-item PHQ-9 check-in followed by a 10-second biometric capture. A psycho-physiological coherence engine cross-checks self-reported mood against autonomic stress markers (HRV, heart rate, respiration, sleep) to detect potential under-reporting. Crewmembers retain sovereign control over what fields are encrypted and transmitted to Flight Surgeons.

• Countermeasures & Pre-EVA Gate: Integrates a 5-level qualitative readiness scale (Perfect, Acceptable, Sufficient, Deficient, Critical) across nutrition, resistive exercise, a 70-day bedrest deconditioning simulator, and a 6-point Pre-EVA clearance gate.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Orbit Care bridges the medical autonomy gap created by deep-space communication delays (up to 20+ minutes one-way to Mars). It prevents minor physiological or psychological anomalies from escalating into mission-critical emergencies. Beyond space exploration, its offline-first architecture, plain-language clinical guidance, and low-resource footprint make it directly transferable to remote clinics, maritime vessels, polar research stations, and disaster-relief zones on Earth.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

• Languages: HTML5, CSS3 (custom responsive HUD design system with Light/Dark mission themes), and modular Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).

• Libraries & Frameworks: Three.js (interactive 3D anatomical mesh rendering and automated diagnostic sweeps), Chart.js (longitudinal multi-sol health trend visualization), and HTML5 Canvas API (real-time PQRST ECG and respiratory waveform rendering).

• Storage & Architecture: Zero-dependency local persistence (localStorage) engineered for offline resilience without cloud reliance.

Creativity & Human-Centered Design

Recognizing that astronauts in microgravity or emergency scenarios may wear gloves or experience high cognitive load, we engineered a Hands-Free Gesture & Dwell HUD allowing touchless navigation (1.2-second hover dwell, directional sweeps, and quick-action gesture triggers). We also replaced intimidating medical jargon with a 5-tier qualitative scale, embedded "What am I looking at?" educational tooltips, and built a non-punitive mental health privacy vault that respects astronaut autonomy while ensuring safety.

Factors Considered

Our team accounted for: non-physician usability under acute stress, historical astronaut reluctance to self-report psychological symptoms due to fear of disqualification, mission-specific environmental stressors and telemetry latency and strict offline availability.
